description: Create the pure, stdlib-only ingest module src/tools/library_ingest.py (Robot *** Settings *** parser, uploaded-set-only resolver, auth/transport contract reasoner, assumption builder, k6 shared-auth-helper renderer, and the budgeted build_library_context orchestrator), and add the max_library_context_chars char-budget key to PIPELINE_SETTINGS. This is the self-contained foundation that FEAT-002 wires in; it does no I/O and no network, and leaves the codebase buildable on its own. Independent of FEAT-002 at build time, but FEAT-002 depends on this module's public API, so this comes first.
steps: Create src/tools/library_ingest.py with `from __future__ import annotations`, stdlib imports only (re, logging, dataclasses, typing, pathlib.PurePosixPath), and `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` (house style from executor.py L38).

Define the dataclasses from design.md 'Module layout and data model': RobotImport(kind, target, alias), ResolvedImport(imp, filename, content) with `resolved` property, AuthContract(login_endpoint, login_method, credential_location, body_shape, token_response_field, later_call_auth, base_paths, secondary_systems, assumptions) with `is_empty`, SecondaryAuthSystem(name, token_endpoint, token_request_shape, token_response_field, attaches_as, applies_to), AuthHelperSpec(path, content, exports), and LibraryContext(resolved, unresolved, aliases, contract, prompt_block, helper_spec, notes) with `is_empty` (prompt_block=='' and helper_spec is None). Use frozen dataclasses where immutable.

Implement parse_robot_settings(content: str) -> list[RobotImport]: no `*** Settings ***` header (case/space-insensitive `re.match(r'\*{3}\s*settings\s*\*{3}', line.strip(), re.I)`) => return []. Enter settings mode on that header, leave on the next `*** ... ***` header. Join `...` continuation lines to the previous logical row. Skip comment (`#`) and blank lines. Split rows with `re.split(r'\s{2,}|\t+', line.strip())`; cells[0] is the keyword (Library/Resource, case-insensitive), cells[1] the target; scan remaining cells for `WITH NAME` (case-insensitive) and tolerate `AS` as a synonym — the token after the marker is the alias. Keep dotted Library tokens verbatim.

Implement resolve_imports(imports, files) -> (list[ResolvedImport], list[RobotImport]): pure function of (imports, files), ZERO I/O (no open/read_text/os). Normalize paths with PurePosixPath after replacing backslashes with '/'. Strategies in order, first hit wins: (1) Resource relative path — candidate filename endswith normalized target OR basenames equal; (2) dotted Library -> path fragment: `clamps.CenxQueryApi` -> fragments `clamps/cenxqueryapi` and `clamps/CenxQueryApi`, match a candidate `.py` path (with .py stripped) ending with either; (3) dotted Library -> defined class: scan candidate .py contents for `^\s*class\s+CenxQueryApi\b` (re.M); (4) plain module -> same path/basename rule as Resources. Alias never affects resolution (key on imp.target). Bounded-transitive: parse resolved .robot resources' Settings and resolve their imports too, to a fixpoint, cap 25 resolved files, never process a filename twice, never follow Python import statements. Unmatched => unresolved list.

Implement derive_contract(resolved) -> AuthContract reading resolved helper CONTENT only, framework-neutral regex heuristics (fields stay None unless positively detected): login endpoint+method with the primary-login selection rule (a login-ish candidate binds to primary iff NOT in the OIDC/Keycloak secondary-shaped helper; the .../token call routes to SecondaryAuthSystem.token_endpoint, never primary; among non-secondary candidates login/session paths beat bare authenticate/token, ties by first-seen; leftovers folded into base_paths) and the method-capture scan window (verb on the same statement as the URL, else nearest verb in the enclosing function body, else None); credential_location='query_param' + body_shape='empty' when creds are URL-encoded into the query (params=/urlencode(/?...username=) with empty body (JSON-body detection only fires when query-param pattern absent); token_response_field via the by-which-helper BINDING RULE (field read in the secondary-shaped helper -> SecondaryAuthSystem.token_response_field, every other read -> primary; single-field + no OIDC shape => primary); later_call_auth='query_param:token' via the ROUTING RULE (('token',t)/token=<t> query attach in a non-secondary helper -> primary; Authorization: Bearer in the secondary-shaped helper -> SecondaryAuthSystem.attaches_as='bearer_header', never overwriting primary); secondary OIDC system (POST to a .../token path consumed with grant_type=password + client_id + application/x-www-form-urlencoded, reads access_token, attaches as bearer, name='oidc'); base_paths de-duped. is_empty True when no login endpoint, no secondary system, no later-call auth.

Implement the assumption builder: the fixed framework-neutral set (cluster/base FQDN, OIDC client_id, realm, service->auth-system mapping, username, password) rendered as one line each of the form `<marker> ASSUMPTION — verify against your API/runtime: <label> -> <env-ref>` with a language-appropriate comment marker (// for JS, # for Python/Robot) and an env reference (__ENV.X for k6, os.environ["X"] for Python) — NEVER a bare value/secret.

Implement build_auth_helper(contract, target_lang, to_name) -> AuthHelperSpec | None: k6 iff target_lang=='javascript' AND 'k6' in to_name.lower() -> render a stdlib-string-templated JS module at path 'lib/auth.js' exporting login() (POST with credentials as query params, empty body, reads the detected token field) and, when a secondary system exists, keycloakToken() (POST form-encoded grant_type=password&client_id=..., reads access_token); every runtime/config value is an __ENV.* reference preceded by the ASSUMPTION marker; exports=('login',) or ('login','keycloakToken'). Any other JavaScript framework (Cypress-JS/Playwright-JS) and any non-JS language -> return None (prompt-context-only).

Implement build_library_context(files, from_name, to_name, target_lang, char_budget) -> LibraryContext: coerce non-string content to ''; parse+resolve across files; derive_contract; build helper_spec via build_auth_helper(contract, target_lang, to_name); assemble the budgeted prompt_block — contract summary ALWAYS included in full and counted first, then raw helper excerpts filling `remaining = max(char_budget - len(summary), 0)` chars with import-matched/auth-signal files ranked first; append import-resolution summary + unresolved notes; end the block with the helper-instruction variant chosen by `helper_spec is not None` ('A shared auth helper (<path>) has been generated ... import its exported functions (<exports>) ...' vs 'The derived auth/transport contract below is advisory; implement login inline ... no shared helper was generated for this target language.'). Return empty LibraryContext (prompt_block='', helper_spec=None, is_empty True) for non-Robot or import-less or no-auth input.

Add the new PIPELINE_SETTINGS key in src/codegen/agent_config.py next to max_context_chars/max_suite_context_chars, using the existing multi-line `#` comment style: `max_library_context_chars` default 6000 with the comment from design.md 'Char-budget cap' (prefer import-matched files).
acceptance_criteria: `python -c "from src.codegen.agent_config import PIPELINE_SETTINGS; assert PIPELINE_SETTINGS['max_library_context_chars'] == 6000"` run from the repo root exits 0.

`python -c "from src.tools import library_ingest as li; imps = li.parse_robot_settings('*** Settings ***
Library    clamps.CenxQueryApi    http://x    WITH NAME    CenxQueryApi
Resource    clamps/cenxrestapi/cenx-rest-api-common.robot
'); print(len(imps))"` prints 2 and the parse exposes the alias CenxQueryApi -> clamps.CenxQueryApi.
library_ingest performs no filesystem or network I/O (no open/os/requests/urllib imports used for I/O); resolver output is a pure function of (imports, files).
verification: Run `python -m py_compile src/tools/library_ingest.py src/codegen/agent_config.py` from the repo root automation-framework-advisor/ and confirm it exits 0.
Run the two inline `python -c` smoke checks above (PIPELINE_SETTINGS key, parser) and confirm expected output.
Grep the module imports to confirm no network/disk libraries are used for I/O (re, logging, dataclasses, typing, pathlib only).
findings:
DONE. Module src/tools/library_ingest.py (pure, stdlib-only: re, logging, dataclasses, pathlib.PurePosixPath, typing — no I/O/network) + PIPELINE_SETTINGS['max_library_context_chars']=6000 added in src/codegen/agent_config.py (right after max_suite_context_chars). All FEAT-001 verification commands pass (py_compile; settings==6000; parser prints 2 with alias CenxQueryApi -> clamps.CenxQueryApi).

PUBLIC API FEAT-002 wires in (all in src.tools.library_ingest):
- build_library_context(files: list[dict], from_name: str, to_name: str, target_lang: str, char_budget: int) -> LibraryContext. This is the orchestrator FEAT-002's ToolExecutor._build_library_context should call, passing char_budget=PIPELINE_SETTINGS['max_library_context_chars']. Returns an EMPTY LibraryContext (prompt_block=='' , helper_spec is None, is_empty True) for non-Robot / import-less / no-auth input — so callers inject nothing and stay byte-for-byte unchanged.
- build_auth_helper(contract: AuthContract, target_lang: str, to_name: str) -> AuthHelperSpec | None. Gates on to_name: k6 iff target_lang=='javascript' AND 'k6' in to_name.lower() -> AuthHelperSpec(path='lib/auth.js', ...); any other JS (Cypress/Playwright) and any non-JS -> None. (Called internally by build_library_context; exposed for tests.)
- parse_robot_settings(content: str) -> list[RobotImport]. [] for non-Robot. RobotImport(kind,target,alias).
- resolve_imports(imports: list[RobotImport], files: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[ResolvedImport], list[RobotImport]] (resolved, unresolved). Pure, zero I/O. ResolvedImport(imp,filename,content) with .resolved property. Note: dotted Library matches a path ending clamps/<pkg>.py OR clamps/<pkg>/<module>.py (parent-dir match), plus class-def fallback.
- derive_contract(resolved: list[ResolvedImport]) -> AuthContract.
- build_assumptions(target_lang: str, *, k6: bool) -> tuple[str,...] (flagged ASSUMPTION lines, env refs only, no secrets).

LibraryContext fields FEAT-002 reads: prompt_block (str, budgeted ready-to-inject block; '' => inject nothing), helper_spec (AuthHelperSpec | None; AuthHelperSpec has .path/.content/.exports — for Groq path do helpers[helper_spec.path]=helper_spec.content; for manual_mode add additive auth_helper={'path','content','exports'}), notes (tuple[str,...] unresolved-import notes; append to summary ONLY when non-empty so empty-context summary stays byte-for-byte identical), is_empty (property == prompt_block=='' and helper_spec is None — the single switch for the no-regression suppression). Also available: ctx.contract (AuthContract), ctx.resolved, ctx.unresolved, ctx.aliases.

prompt_block ends with the helper-instruction variant chosen on helper_spec is not None: contains the substring 'has been generated' when a helper exists, else the inline-login advisory variant (so the prompt never tells the model to import a helper that was not emitted).

FEAT-002 TODO (NOT done here, per scope): _build_system_prompt gets keyword-defaulted library_block='' param injected after ctx; ToolExecutor._build_library_context wrapper (lazy import, try/except Exception -> empty LibraryContext); convert_multi_file + manual_mode.build_multi_file_conversion_brief wiring.
